response.text:
The empirical frequency table is not included in the prompt, so the requested numerical Pearson statistic, p-value, observed \(\bar X\), and \(z\)-value cannot be uniquely computed from the information given. Those quantities depend on the observed counts in the table.

That said, the null distribution and the required calculations are as follows.

Let \(O_x\) be the observed frequency among the 100 trials for \(X=x,\ x=0,\dots,6\). Under uniformity,

\[
X\sim \mathrm{Hypergeometric}(N=49,K=25,n=6),
\]

so

\[
p_x=P(X=x)=\frac{\binom{25}{x}\binom{24}{6-x}}{\binom{49}{6}},\qquad x=0,\dots,6.
\]

The null probabilities are approximately

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6\\
\hline
p_x & 0.00963 & 0.07599 & 0.22796 & 0.33290 & 0.24967 & 0.09119 & 0.01266
\end{array}
\]

so the expected counts out of 100 are

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6\\
\hline
E_x & 0.963 & 7.599 & 22.796 & 33.290 & 24.967 & 9.119 & 1.266
\end{array}
\]

Because the expected counts for \(x=0\) and \(x=6\) are small, a standard Pearson chi-square test would usually combine tails, for example using categories

\[
\{0,1\},\quad \{2\},\quad \{3\},\quad \{4\},\quad \{5,6\}.
\]

Then the expected counts are

\[
8.561,\quad 22.796,\quad 33.290,\quad 24.967,\quad 10.385.
\]

The Pearson statistic would be

\[
\chi^2
=
\frac{(O_{0}+O_{1}-8.561)^2}{8.561}
+
\frac{(O_2-22.796)^2}{22.796}
+
\frac{(O_3-33.290)^2}{33.290}
+
\frac{(O_4-24.967)^2}{24.967}
+
\frac{(O_5+O_6-10.385)^2}{10.385}.
\]

Since no parameters are estimated, the degrees of freedom would be

\[
5-1=4.
\]

Thus the p-value would be

\[
p=P(\chi^2_4\ge \chi^2_{\text{obs}}).
\]

For part (2), the observed sample mean is

\[
\bar X_{\text{obs}}
=
\frac{1}{100}\sum_{x=0}^6 xO_x.
\]

Under the null,

\[
E(\bar X)=\frac{6\cdot 25}{49}=3.061\approx 3.06,
\]

and the problem gives

\[
\operatorname{SD}(\bar X)=0.116.
\]

Therefore the \(z\)-statistic is

\[
z
=
\frac{\bar X_{\text{obs}}-3.06}{0.116}.
\]

Without the empirical frequencies \(O_0,\dots,O_6\), the numerical values of \(\chi^2\), the p-value, \(\bar X_{\text{obs}}\), and \(z\) cannot be computed. Consequently, one also cannot conclude from the pasted information alone whether the gadget produces uniform results.
